big_picture_notes: The Psalter is a curated anthology of 150 distinct poems, songs, and prayers organized into five Books (Pss 1–41; 42–72; 73–89; 90–106; 107–150). Each of the first four Books ends with an explicit doxology and the whole concludes with Psalm 150 as a grand doxology. Within this five‑book structure, smaller editorially placed collections appear (e.g., Davidic psalms, Sons of Korah, Asaph, Songs of Ascents). For memorization, each psalm is a complete literary unit (scene). Longer psalms should not be arbitrarily split, though internal strophes (often marked by Selah, speaker/audience shifts, or thematic turns) can serve as day‑by‑day chunks. Books I–V trace a theological arc from the struggle of the righteous king (I), through the Elohistic collection (II), the national crisis (III), the answer 'YHWH reigns' (IV), to the climactic Hallelujah and pilgrim ascent (V).

stories.story_title: Book I – The Struggle of the Righteous King
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Textually defined 'Book I' framed by gateway Psalms 1–2 (Torah joy and Messianic kingship) and closed by the explicit doxology at 41:13. Predominantly Davidic, dominated by individual laments and trust, the righteous one surrounded by the wicked. Start (1:1): thematic prologue 'Blessed is the man...' End (41:13): 'Blessed be the LORD... Amen and Amen.' Literary Glue: Davidic superscriptions, lament→trust trajectories, righteous vs wicked motif.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 1 – The Two Ways
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Wisdom prologue to the whole Psalter; antithetical parallelism — righteous as watered tree (1-3) vs. wicked as chaff (4-5), sealed by the summary verdict (6).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 2 – The Nations Rage
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Royal psalm, movement 1: earth's kings conspire to break the cords of the LORD and His Anointed.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 2 – Enthroned in Heaven Laughs
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Movement 2 (speaker = the LORD): heaven's derisive laugh, then the decree 'I have installed My King on Zion.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 2 – You Are My Son
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Movement 3 (speaker = the Son): the begotten-decree and the iron-scepter inheritance of the nations.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 2 – Kiss the Son
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Movement 4 (narrator): wisdom-warning to kings, closing on the beatitude 'Blessed are all who take refuge in Him.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 3 – A Shield Around Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Absalom-flight lament: complaint at swelling foes (1-2) answered by confidence in the LORD who lifts the head (3-4); two Selahs.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 3 – I Lie Down and Sleep
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Remembrance of sustained sleep (5-6) turning to petition 'Arise, O LORD' and the creed 'Salvation belongs to the LORD' (7-8).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 4 – Answer Me When I Call
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Evening companion to Ps 3: plea to the God of righteousness (1) and rebuke to the proud — 'be angry, yet do not sin' (2-4); Selah strophes.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 4 – Sleep in Peace
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: From offered sacrifices and the lifted light of God's face (5-7) to the psalm's resting note: 'I will lie down and sleep in peace' (8).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 5 – Morning Plea for Audience
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Lament opening: 'Give ear… consider my groaning,' framed by the dawn vigil — 'in the morning… I lay my plea before You.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 5 – No Evil Dwells with You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Meditation on God's character: He hates iniquity and bloodshed (4-6), yet the psalmist enters His house by abundant devotion (7).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 5 – Lead Me in Your Righteousness
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Petition against open-grave throats (8-10) closing in the blessing and shield of favor over the righteous (11-12).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 6 – Do Not Rebuke Me in Anger
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: First penitential psalm: plea against wrathful discipline, 'how long, O LORD?', begging deliverance for devotion's sake.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 6 – Weary with Groaning
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Depth of the lament: no praise in Sheol (5), the bed flooded with nightly tears, eyes failing from grief (6-7).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 6 – Depart from Me, Workers of Evil
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The confident pivot: the LORD has heard the weeping; enemies turn back in sudden, shamed disgrace.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 7 – Refuge from the Lion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Shiggaion opening: take refuge in God lest the pursuer shred the soul like a lion with none to rescue.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 7 – The Oath of Innocence
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Self-imprecation: if guilt is on his hands, let the enemy trample him to the dust; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 7 – Arise, O Righteous Judge
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Petition for the divine assize: the LORD takes His seat over the peoples and searches hearts and minds.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 7 – God Has Bent His Bow
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Confidence in the righteous Judge who, against the unrepentant, sharpens His sword and readies fiery arrows.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 7 – Fallen into His Own Pit
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Poetic justice — the wicked conceives trouble and falls into the pit he dug (14-16) — answered by the vow of praise (17).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 8 – Majesty Above the Heavens
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Inclusio opens: 'how majestic is Your name,' praise ordained from the mouths of infants to silence the foe.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 8 – What Is Man?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The heart of the hymn: gazing at moon and stars, the wonder that God crowns frail man with glory and honor.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 8 – Crowned to Rule
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Dominion over flocks, beasts, birds, and fish (6-8), closing on the repeated refrain of God's majestic name (9).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 9 – I Will Recount Your Wonders
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Acrostic thanksgiving opens (Aleph–Beth): whole-hearted praise and joy in the Most High.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 9 – The Enemy Comes to Ruin
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Past deliverance: enemies stumble and perish, nations rebuked, their very name and memory erased forever.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 9 – The LORD Reigns for Judgment
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's eternal throne of justice — a stronghold for the oppressed and a refuge for all who know His name.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 9 – The Avenger Remembers the Afflicted
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Call to sing of Zion's King (11-12) turning to personal plea — lift me from the gates of death (13-14).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 9 – The Nations in Their Own Net
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Nations snared by their own hands (15-16, Higgaion Selah); the needy not forgotten; 'let the nations know they are but men' (17-20).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 10 – Why Do You Stand Far Off?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Companion lament: the cry of God's apparent absence while the proud hunt the needy.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 10 – The Boast of the Wicked
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Portrait of the godless man — boasting in greed, 'there is no God,' mouth full of cursing and deceit.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 10 – Lurking Like a Lion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The predator in ambush, crushing the helpless, telling himself 'God has forgotten… never sees.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 10 – Arise, O LORD, Lift Your Hand
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Petition: break the arm of the wicked; You, helper of the fatherless, see and repay the trouble.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 10 – The LORD Is King Forever
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Resolution: the eternal King vindicates the fatherless and oppressed so that earthly men strike terror no more.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 11 – Flee Like a Bird?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Confronting the counsel of despair: 'if the foundations are destroyed, what can the righteous do?'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 11 – The LORD in His Holy Temple
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The answer of faith: the enthroned LORD tests the righteous, rains judgment on the wicked, and the upright will see His face.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 12 – Flattering Lips and Double Hearts
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Lament for a faithless generation of smooth, boastful tongues; plea that the LORD cut them off.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 12 – Words Pure as Refined Silver
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The LORD's oracle to arise for the oppressed (5), and the contrast of His flawless words with the wicked who strut about (6-8).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 13 – How Long, O LORD?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Compact lament: the fourfold 'how long' (1-2) moving through petition (3-4) to trust and song (5-6).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 14 – The Fool Says, 'No God'
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Indictment of universal corruption — the LORD looks down and finds none who do good, not one.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 14 – Salvation Out of Zion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The evildoers who devour God's people are overwhelmed with dread; closing longing for restoration from Zion.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 15 – Who May Dwell on Your Holy Hill
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Entrance liturgy: the character of the guest God welcomes — blameless walk, truthful tongue, no bribe; 'never shaken.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 16 – Apart from You No Good Thing
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Miktam of refuge: the LORD as the only good, the saints as delight, with no libations poured to other gods.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 16 – The LORD Is My Portion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Pleasant boundary lines and a secure lot (5-6); the LORD set always before him, He will not be shaken (7-8).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 16 – You Will Not Abandon My Soul
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Confidence into resurrection hope — 'nor let Your Holy One see decay' — and the path of life with eternal pleasures.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 17 – Hear My Righteous Plea
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Prayer of integrity: lips free of deceit, tried in the night and found resolved not to sin; steps held to God's paths.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 17 – The Apple of Your Eye
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Petition for wondrous love — 'keep me as the apple of Your eye, hide me in the shadow of Your wings' from assailants.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 17 – Like a Lion Hungry for Prey
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The encircling foes: callous hearts, arrogant mouths, set to cast him down like a lurking young lion.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 17 – I Will Behold Your Face
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Closing contrast: men of the world whose portion is this life (13-14) against the psalmist who awakes satisfied in God's likeness (15).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – I Love You, O LORD My Strength
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Royal thanksgiving opens: a cascade of refuge-titles — rock, fortress, deliverer, shield, horn of salvation.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – The Cords of Death
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Distress: the snares of Sheol entangle, and from His temple He hears the cry.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – The Earth Shook and Quaked
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Theophany begins — smoke and consuming fire, the heavens parted as He descends.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – He Mounted a Cherub and Flew
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The storm-rider: darkness His canopy, hailstones and coals breaking from His brightness.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – The LORD Thundered from Heaven
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Most High's voice; sea-channels and world-foundations laid bare at the blast of His breath.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – He Drew Me Out of Deep Waters
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The rescue: reaching from on high to take hold, bringing him into the open 'because He delighted in me.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – Rewarded for Clean Hands
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The righteousness motif — kept the ways of the LORD, blameless before Him, repaid for clean hands.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – With the Faithful You Show Yourself Faithful
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Wisdom couplet on reciprocity: faithful, blameless, pure, shrewd — God saves the afflicted, humbles the haughty.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – You Light My Lamp
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Empowerment: God lights the darkness, lets him scale a wall; His way perfect, His word flawless, a shield to all who trust.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – He Trains My Hands for Battle
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: 'Who is God besides the LORD?' — the Rock who arms with strength, makes feet like a deer, bends a bow of bronze.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – Your Right Hand Upholds Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The shield of salvation and broadened path (35-36) enabling pursuit of the enemy until consumed (37).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – Subdued Beneath My Feet
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Victory: foes crushed and unable to rise, armed with strength, enemies put to flight.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – Head of the Nations
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Enemies cry with none to save (41-42); made head of nations as foreigners cower and come trembling (43-45).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – The LORD Lives!
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Doxological turn: blessed be the Rock, the God who avenges and rescues from violent men.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 18 – Loving Devotion to His Anointed
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Closing vow to praise among the nations, sealed by covenant — 'to David and his descendants forever.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 19 – The Heavens Declare the Glory of God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: General revelation: the wordless speech of sky pouring forth knowledge (1-4), the sun like a bridegroom running its circuit (5-6).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 19 – The Law of the LORD Is Perfect
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Special revelation: six poised lines on law, testimony, precepts, commandment, fear, and judgments — reviving, sure, right, radiant.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 19 – Sweeter than Honey
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Torah more precious than gold (10-11), the prayer to be cleansed of hidden and willful sins (12-13), closing on acceptable words and meditation (14).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 20 – May the LORD Answer You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Intercession for the king before battle: help from the sanctuary, accepted offerings, and granted petitions; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 20 – Some Trust in Chariots
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Confidence — 'now I know the LORD saves His anointed'; the contrast of horses with the name of the LORD; 'O LORD, save the king.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 21 – The King Rejoices in Your Strength
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Thanksgiving for the king: granted his heart's desire, crowned with gold, given length of days forever; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 21 – Splendor and Majesty
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The king's glory and everlasting blessings, grounded in trust — 'through the devotion of the Most High he will not be shaken.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 21 – Your Hand Will Find Your Foes
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Address shifting to judgment of enemies in the fiery furnace of His appearing (8-12), closing 'Be exalted, O LORD' (13).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 22 – My God, Why Have You Forsaken Me?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The cry of dereliction: forsaken and unanswered by day and night — the opening of the great passion psalm.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 22 – Yet You Are Holy
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The turn to the fathers' trust: enthroned on Israel's praises, He delivered those who cried and trusted.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 22 – Scorned and Despised
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: 'I am a worm, not a man' — mockers shake their heads, taunting 'let the LORD deliver him.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 22 – From My Mother's Womb
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Appeal to lifelong dependence from birth, with the petition 'be not far from me, for trouble is near.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 22 – Poured Out Like Water
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The suffering deepens: bulls of Bashan, lions' jaws, disjointed bones, melting heart, 'You lay me in the dust of death.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 22 – They Pierced My Hands and Feet
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The crucifixion imagery: encircling dogs, counted bones, garments divided and cast for by lot.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 22 – Deliver My Soul from the Sword
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The last cries for rescue from sword, lion, and wild oxen — ending 'You have answered me!'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 22 – I Will Proclaim Your Name
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The vow of praise in the assembly; the LORD has not despised the affliction of the afflicted.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 22 – The Ends of the Earth Will Turn
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Widening praise: the poor satisfied, all the earth's families bowing, for dominion belongs to the LORD.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 22 – To a People Yet Unborn
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The cosmic reach into the future — posterity will serve Him and proclaim His righteousness, 'all that He has done.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 23 – The LORD Is My Shepherd
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Complete shepherd psalm: green pastures and quiet waters, the valley of shadow, the prepared table, and dwelling in the house of the LORD forever.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 24 – The Earth Is the LORD's
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Creation claim: the world and all its dwellers belong to Him who founded it on the seas.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 24 – Clean Hands and a Pure Heart
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Entrance liturgy: who may ascend the hill of the LORD — those who do not lift their soul to an idol; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 24 – Lift Up Your Heads, O Gates
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Antiphonal procession: the ancient doors open for the King of Glory, 'the LORD of Hosts'; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 25 – To You I Lift Up My Soul
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Acrostic opens: trust that none who wait for the LORD will be put to shame.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 25 – Show Me Your Ways
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Petition for guidance and mercy — 'remember not the sins of my youth' — grounded in the LORD's age-old compassion.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 25 – Good and Upright Is the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: He guides the humble and teaches sinners; all His ways loving and faithful to covenant-keepers.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 25 – The Friendship of the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Plea for pardon of great iniquity (11) and the promise that the LORD confides His covenant to those who fear Him (12-14).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 25 – Turn to Me, I Am Lonely
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Eyes ever on the LORD (15) amid loneliness, multiplying troubles, and the plea to take away all sins.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 25 – Redeem Israel, O God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Final petition against many fierce enemies, sheltering in integrity, widening to the nation: 'Redeem Israel from all its distress.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 26 – Vindicate Me, for I Have Walked in Integrity
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Plea of the innocent: 'test me… examine my heart,' walking in God's truth and devotion.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 26 – I Do Not Sit with the Deceitful
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Protestation of separation from the wicked, balanced by washed hands going about the altar in thanksgiving.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 26 – I Love the House Where You Dwell
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Love for God's dwelling (8) with the plea not to be swept away with sinners (9-10); 'my feet stand on level ground' (11-12).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 27 – The LORD Is My Light and Salvation
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Bold confidence: 'whom shall I fear?' — though an army encamps, the heart will not fear.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 27 – One Thing I Have Asked
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The single desire to dwell in the house of the LORD and gaze on His beauty; hidden in His shelter, lifted high on a rock.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 27 – Your Face, O LORD, I Will Seek
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The turn to petition — 'hide not Your face' — resting on the promise 'though father and mother forsake me, the LORD will receive me.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 27 – Wait for the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Plea against false witnesses (11-12), the certainty of seeing His goodness in the land of the living (13), and the closing charge to wait courageously (14).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 28 – Be Not Deaf to Me, O My Rock
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Cry against the silence of God, lifting hands toward His holy sanctuary.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 28 – Do Not Drag Me Away with the Wicked
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Plea to be spared the fate of the deceitful, who will be torn down for ignoring the works of the LORD.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 28 – The LORD Is My Strength and Shield
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Sudden praise — the cry has been heard (6-7) — widening to intercession: 'Save Your people… shepherd them forever' (8-9).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 29 – Ascribe to the LORD Glory
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Summons to the heavenly beings to worship in the splendor of holiness.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 29 – The Voice of the LORD over the Waters
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The thunder-theophany: His voice breaks the cedars of Lebanon and makes the mountains skip.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 29 – The Voice That Shakes the Wilderness
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Flames of fire, the shaken Wilderness of Kadesh, the twisted oaks — and in His temple all cry, 'Glory!'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 29 – Enthroned over the Flood
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The LORD enthroned as eternal King who gives His people strength and blesses them with peace.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 30 – You Lifted Me Up
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Temple-dedication thanksgiving: healed and drawn up from Sheol, not letting foes rejoice.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 30 – Joy Comes in the Morning
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Call to the saints to praise: His anger fleeting, His favor a lifetime — 'weeping may stay the night, but joy comes in the morning.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 30 – When You Hid Your Face
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: From false security (6) to dismay when God hid His face (7), and the bargaining cry from the Pit (8-10).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 30 – Mourning into Dancing
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The reversal: sackcloth stripped and joy put on, that the heart may sing and give thanks forever.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 31 – In You I Take Refuge
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Opening trust: 'be my rock of refuge,' led and guided for the sake of His name.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 31 – Into Your Hands I Commit My Spirit
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Freed from the hidden net (4); the entrusting word later spoken by Christ (5); hatred of idols, trust in the LORD (6).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 31 – Wasting Away with Grief
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Gladness in His devotion (7-8) turning to lament — eyes failing, life consumed, bones wasting (9-10).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 31 – A Broken Vessel
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Social desolation: a disgrace to neighbors, dreaded by friends, forgotten like the dead, surrounded by terror and plots.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 31 – My Times Are in Your Hands
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The pivot of trust — 'You are my God; my times are in Your hands' — with the plea for a shining face.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 31 – How Great Is Your Goodness
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Plea against lying lips (17-18) leading to wonder at the goodness stored up and the hiding place of God's presence (19-20).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 31 – Be Strong, All Who Hope in the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Blessing for devotion shown in a besieged city (21-22), closing with the charge to love the LORD and take courage (23-24).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 32 – Blessed Is He Whose Sin Is Covered
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Maskil beatitude on forgiveness — the man against whom the LORD counts no iniquity.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 32 – When I Kept Silent
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The cost of concealment — wasting bones and heavy hand (3-4) — broken by confession and instant forgiveness (5); Selahs.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 32 – You Are My Hiding Place
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The godly pray while God may be found; He is the hiding place surrounding with songs of deliverance; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 32 – I Will Instruct You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's promise to teach the way (8), the warning not to be like a senseless mule (9), and the contrast of the wicked's sorrows with the joy of the upright (10-11).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 33 – Sing to Him a New Song
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Hymn opening: fitting praise from the upright, with harp and ten-stringed lyre and a shout of joy.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 33 – By the Word of the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's trustworthy word and love (4-5) by which the heavens were made and the seas gathered into storehouses (6-7).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 33 – He Spoke, and It Came to Be
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The earth summoned to fear (8-9); the LORD frustrates the nations' plans, but His counsel stands forever — 'blessed is the nation whose God is the LORD' (10-12).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 33 – The LORD Looks Down from Heaven
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The all-seeing Maker who fashions every heart and weighs all their works.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 33 – No King Saved by His Army
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The vanity of horse and army for salvation (16-17); the LORD's eye is on those who hope in His devotion, to keep them alive in famine (18-19).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 33 – Our Soul Waits for the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Closing confidence — He is our help and shield — with the prayer that His devotion rest on those who hope in Him.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 34 – I Will Bless the LORD at All Times
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Acrostic thanksgiving opens with the summons to magnify the LORD together; the afflicted invited to rejoice.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 34 – Taste and See
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Sought the LORD and was delivered (4); faces radiant, unashamed (5-6); the angel of the LORD encamps around those who fear Him (7).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 34 – Those Who Fear Him Lack Nothing
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: 'Taste and see that the LORD is good' (8); even young lions go hungry, but seekers of the LORD lack no good thing (9-10).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 34 – Keep Your Tongue from Evil
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Wisdom instruction: who desires life must keep tongue from evil, turn from evil, and pursue peace.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 34 – The LORD Is Near the Brokenhearted
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The eyes and ears of the LORD toward the righteous (15-17); 'the LORD is near to the brokenhearted… saves the contrite in spirit' (18).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 34 – Not One of His Bones Broken
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Many afflictions but full deliverance (19), the protected unbroken bones (20), and the redemption of His servants from condemnation (21-22).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 35 – Contend with My Opponents
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Lament as appeal to the divine Warrior: 'take up shield and spear… say to my soul, I am your salvation.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 35 – Like Chaff in the Wind
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Imprecation that those who seek his life be driven back like chaff, the angel of the LORD pursuing.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 35 – Caught in Their Own Net
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The hidden net springing on its makers (7-8) and the rejoicing response of every bone, 'Who is like You, O LORD?' (9-10).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 35 – They Repay Evil for Good
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The betrayal: hostile witnesses repay the kindness he showed when he mourned and fasted for them in their illness.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 35 – Glee at My Stumbling
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Mockers gathering in malice and gnashing teeth (15-16), the cry 'how long?', and the vow to thank Him in the great assembly (17-18).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 35 – Aha, Aha! Our Eyes Have Seen
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The gloating of treacherous foes who do not speak peace but devise deceit against the quiet of the land.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 35 – You Have Seen It, O LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Plea that the LORD not stay silent but awake to vindicate by His righteousness.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 35 – Shout for Joy at My Vindication
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: That gloaters be clothed in shame (25-26) while those who favor his cause rejoice (27); closing in all-day praise (28).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 36 – No Fear of God Before His Eyes
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Oracle on the wicked: flattering self-deceit, deceitful speech, and bedtime plotting of a path that is not good.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 36 – Your Loving Devotion Reaches the Heavens
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The great contrast — God's love to the clouds, righteousness like mountains (5-6), the feast of His house and 'the fountain of life; in Your light we see light' (7-9).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 36 – There the Evildoers Lie Fallen
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Prayer to extend His devotion to the upright (10-11), sealed by the vision of the proud thrown down, unable to rise (12).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 37 – Do Not Fret Because of Evildoers
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Acrostic wisdom opens: do not envy the wicked, for they wither quickly like grass.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 37 – Delight Yourself in the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The fourfold counsel — trust, delight, commit, be still — and the promise He will bring forth your righteousness like the dawn.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 37 – Refrain from Anger
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Be still and wait patiently; do not fret over those who prosper, for evildoers will be cut off but the hopeful inherit the land.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 37 – The Meek Will Inherit the Land
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: 'Yet a little while' and the wicked are gone, while the meek delight in abundant prosperity.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 37 – Their Swords Pierce Their Own Hearts
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The wicked scheme and gnash (12-13), draw sword and bow against the poor (14), but their own weapons turn on them (15).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 37 – Better the Little of the Righteous
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The little of the righteous over the wealth of the wicked (16-17); the LORD knows the days of the blameless (18-19); the wicked vanish like smoke (20).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 37 – The Steps of a Man Are Ordered
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The generous righteous inherit the land (21-22); their steps ordered by the LORD, upheld by His hand when they fall (23-24).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 37 – I Was Young and Now Am Old
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The testimony of long life — the righteous never abandoned (25-26) — grounded in the LORD who loves justice and preserves His saints (27-28).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 37 – The Law in His Heart
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The righteous inherit the land forever (29); the mouth that utters wisdom and the law kept in the heart (30-31).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 37 – Wait and Keep His Way
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Though the wicked lie in wait (32-33), the LORD will not abandon the righteous to their power; wait and you will see the wicked cut off (34).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 37 – The Wicked Flourishing, Then Gone
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A ruthless man flourishing like a green tree, then vanished (35-36); the future of the man of peace against the cutoff of transgressors (37-38).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 37 – Their Stronghold in Trouble
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Closing creed: salvation of the righteous is from the LORD, their refuge and rescue.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 38 – Do Not Rebuke Me in Your Anger
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Penitential lament: God's arrows and heavy hand (1-2), no soundness because of sin, iniquities a crushing burden (3-4).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 38 – Festering Wounds
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The bodily ruin of guilt — foul wounds, bowed low, burning pain, groaning in anguish of heart.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 38 – My Friends Stand Aloof
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Every desire laid bare before God (9), failing strength (10), friends and kinsmen keeping their distance while enemies plot (11-12).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 38 – Like a Deaf and Mute Man
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Silent before slander (13-14), waiting on the LORD to answer (15), lest the enemy gloat when his foot slips (16).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 38 – I Confess My Iniquity
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Ready to fall and confessing sin (17-18) while enemies repay good with evil and attack his pursuit of good (19-20).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 38 – Come Quickly to Help Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing cry not to be forsaken: 'come quickly to help me, O Lord my Savior.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 39 – I Will Guard My Mouth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Resolve to keep silent before the wicked (1-2) until the inner fire burns and he must speak (3).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 39 – The Measure of My Days
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Meditation on mortality: life as a handbreadth, every man a mere breath who bustles in vain; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 39 – My Hope Is in You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Hope turned to God (7), plea for deliverance from transgressions (8), silence under God's hand (9-10), and the moth-like fading of man (11); Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 39 – A Stranger Like All My Fathers
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing plea of the sojourner that God turn His gaze and let him be cheered before he departs.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 40 – He Put a New Song in My Mouth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Thanksgiving: lifted from the miry pit and set on a rock, given a new song that many will see and fear.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 40 – Your Wonders Are More Than I Can Count
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The beatitude on trust (4) and the wonder at God's innumerable works and plans (5).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 40 – I Delight to Do Your Will
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Sacrifice not desired but opened ears (6); 'Here I am… I delight to do Your will; Your law is within my heart' (7-8).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 40 – I Did Not Seal My Lips
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The proclamation of righteousness, faithfulness, and salvation, unconcealed, in the great assembly.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 40 – Evils Without Number Surround Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The lament pivot: mercy implored (11) as countless evils and sins overtake him (12); 'hurry, O LORD, to help me' (13).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 40 – I Am Poor and Needy
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Imprecation on those who seek his life (14-15), joy for all who seek God (16), and the closing cry, 'do not delay' (17).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 41 – Blessed Is He Who Cares for the Poor
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Beatitude on compassion: the LORD protects, preserves, and sustains him on his sickbed.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 41 – When Will He Die?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Confession 'heal me, for I have sinned' (4) against the malice of enemies who wish his death and spread slander (5-6).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 41 – My Close Friend Lifted His Heel
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The deepest wound of betrayal — the trusted friend who shared his bread has turned against him.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 41 – From Everlasting to Everlasting
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Plea to be raised up (10-11), upheld in integrity (12), sealed by the doxology that closes Book I: 'Blessed be the LORD… Amen and Amen' (13).

stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Defined by the doxology at 72:18–20 (with colophon v. 20). Opens with Sons of Korah cluster (42–49) and shows preference for Elohim over YHWH. Start (42:1): 'As a deer pants...' End (72:18–20): double doxology + 'The prayers of David... are ended.' Literary Glue: Korahite/Asaph collections; Elohistic diction.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 42 – As the Deer Pants
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Korahite Maskil; opening strophe of the 42–43 unit: thirst for the living God amid taunts, sealed by the refrain 'Why are you downcast, O my soul?' (5).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 42 – Deep Calls to Deep
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: From the land of Jordan and Hermon (6-7) the despairing soul recalls God's song by night and repeats the refrain (11).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 43 – Send Out Your Light and Truth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Conclusion of the 42–43 poem: plea for vindication and for the light that leads to God's altar, closing on the third refrain (5).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 44 – We Have Heard with Our Ears
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Communal psalm opens with the fathers' testimony: the land won not by sword but by God's right hand and the light of His face.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 44 – You Are My King, O God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Present confession of dependence — not trusting bow or sword — boasting in God's name all day long; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 44 – But You Have Rejected Us
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The bitter turn: routed before the foe, given up like sheep to be devoured, sold for nothing.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 44 – A Byword Among the Nations
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The reproach of defeat — a mockery to neighbors, shame covering the face before scorner and reviler.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 44 – Yet We Have Not Forgotten You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The protest of innocence: hearts not turned back though crushed in the lair of jackals and covered with darkness.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 44 – As Sheep to Be Slaughtered
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Appeal to the God who knows the heart's secrets — 'for Your sake we face death all day long.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 44 – Wake Up, O Lord!
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The audacious closing cry against God's apparent sleep: 'Rise up; be our help! Redeem us for Your loving devotion.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 45 – My Heart Is Stirred by a Noble Theme
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Royal wedding song opens: the poet's tongue a ready pen, addressing the king graced and blessed by God.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 45 – Ride Forth in Splendor
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The warrior-king summoned to ride for truth and justice, his arrows piercing the hearts of his foes.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 45 – Your Throne, O God, Endures Forever
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The psalm's height: the king addressed as God, anointed above his companions with the oil of joy (quoted of the Son in Heb 1).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 45 – Garments Fragrant with Myrrh
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The wedding scene: ivory palaces, glad harps, and the queen in gold of Ophir at the king's right hand.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 45 – Forget Your People, O Daughter
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Counsel to the bride to leave her father's house so the king will desire her beauty, with tribute from Tyre.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 45 – Led to the King with Joy
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The glorious procession of the gold-robed princess and her companions into the palace.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 45 – Your Name Through All Generations
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Closing promise to the king: sons to succeed him as princes, and a name praised by the nations forever.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 46 – God Is Our Refuge and Strength
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: 'An ever-present help in trouble'; no fear though earth gives way and mountains fall into the sea; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 46 – A River Gladdens the City of God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The unmoved city where the Most High dwells (4-5); nations rage and melt, but 'the LORD of Hosts is with us' (6-7); Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 46 – Be Still and Know That I Am God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: 'Come, see the works of the LORD' who makes wars cease (8-9), and the divine self-declaration of exaltation (10-11); Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 47 – Clap Your Hands, All Peoples
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Enthronement summons: the great King over all the earth who subdues nations and chooses Jacob's inheritance; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 47 – God Has Ascended
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God ascends amid shouts and horn-blast (5); the fivefold 'sing praises' (6-7); 'God reigns… seated on His holy throne' (8-9).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 48 – Mount Zion, the City of the Great King
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Zion-hymn: great is the LORD in His city, beautiful in loftiness, His citadels a proven fortress.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 48 – The Kings Saw and Fled
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The assembled kings seized with labor-pangs of terror (4-6); ships of Tarshish wrecked; 'God will establish her forever' (7-8); Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 48 – We Contemplate Your Devotion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Within the temple, meditation on God's love and the praise of His name reaching to the ends of the earth.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 48 – Walk About Zion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Survey her towers and ramparts to tell the next generation: 'this God is our God forever, our guide even to death.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 49 – Hear This, All You Peoples
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Wisdom psalm opens to low and high alike — the sage inclines his ear to a riddle solved with the harp.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 49 – No Man Can Redeem His Brother
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The riddle stated: wealth cannot buy off death, for the ransom of a soul is forever beyond price.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 49 – Wise and Fool Alike Perish
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: All die and leave their wealth to others; despite named estates, man is 'like the beasts that perish.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 49 – God Will Redeem My Soul
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The fate of the self-confident — death their shepherd (13-14, Selah) — against the hope 'God will redeem my life from Sheol' (15).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 49 – Do Not Be Afraid When a Man Grows Rich
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The refrain-conclusion: the rich carry nothing away, and the man without understanding is like the beasts that perish.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 50 – God Summons the Earth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Asaph's covenant-lawsuit opens with theophany: from Zion God shines forth, fire and tempest before Him.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 50 – Gather to Me My Saints
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God calls heaven and earth as witnesses to judge His covenant people; the heavens proclaim His righteousness; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 50 – The Cattle on a Thousand Hills
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The first charge: God needs no bull from the stall, for every beast of the forest is already His.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 50 – Sacrifice a Thank Offering
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: What God desires is thanksgiving and kept vows — 'call upon Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 50 – What Right Have You to Recite My Statutes?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The case against the wicked who mouth the covenant while befriending thieves and adulterers.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 50 – You Slander Your Own Brother
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The tongue harnessed to deceit; God's silence mistaken for approval — 'now I rebuke you to your face.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 50 – Consider This, You Who Forget God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing warning and promise: the thank offering honors Him, and the rightly ordered way sees His salvation.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 51 – Have Mercy on Me, O God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The great penitential opens after Nathan's rebuke: appeal to God's devotion to blot out and wash away sin.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 51 – Against You Only Have I Sinned
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Confession laid bare — sin ever before him, sinful from conception, yet God desires truth in the inmost being.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 51 – Whiter Than Snow
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Plea for cleansing with hyssop and for the crushed bones to rejoice, that God would hide His face from sin.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 51 – Create in Me a Clean Heart
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The heart of the prayer: a renewed spirit, not cast from His presence, the joy of salvation restored.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 51 – Then I Will Teach Transgressors
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The vow that flows from pardon: teaching sinners, singing of righteousness, lips opened to declare His praise.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 51 – A Broken and Contrite Heart
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The sacrifice God will not despise is not burnt offering but a broken spirit.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 51 – Build Up the Walls of Jerusalem
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing turn to Zion's good, when right sacrifices will again delight Him.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 52 – Why Boast of Evil, O Mighty Man?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Indictment of Doeg the informer: a tongue like a sharpened razor that loves devouring falsehood; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 52 – God Will Bring You Down
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The certain ruin of the man who made wealth, not God, his refuge — at which the righteous will look and fear.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 52 – Like an Olive Tree in the House of God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The contrast of the psalmist: flourishing and trusting in God's devotion forever, waiting on His good name.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 53 – The Fool Says, 'No God'
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Elohistic counterpart to Psalm 14: universal corruption, God looking down from heaven, and the longing for salvation out of Zion.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 54 – Save Me by Your Name
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Plea when the Ziphites betrayed David: ruthless strangers with no regard for God seek his life; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 54 – Surely God Is My Helper
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Confidence that God sustains the soul and will repay enemies, sealed by a freewill sacrifice of praise.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 55 – Listen to My Prayer, O God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Lament opens in restless complaint at the voice and pressure of the wicked who bring disaster.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 55 – Oh, for Wings Like a Dove!
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Terror of death within (4-5) and the longing to fly far away to rest in the wilderness (6-8); Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 55 – Violence and Strife in the City
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Prayer to confound the conspirators' speech, for malice and oppression never leave the streets.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 55 – It Is You, My Companion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The wound of betrayal — not an enemy but a close friend with whom he walked to the house of God.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 55 – But I Call to God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Imprecation that death seize the treacherous (15) against the trust 'I call to God, and the LORD saves me' (16).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 55 – Morning, Noon, and Night I Cry
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Threefold daily prayer heard; the One enthroned for the ages will humble those with no fear of God; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 55 – Smooth as Butter, Yet Drawn Swords
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The traitor's covenant-breaking: speech softer than oil, but war in his heart.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 55 – Cast Your Burden on the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing wisdom-word: He sustains the righteous, while men of bloodshed will not live out half their days.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 56 – When I Am Afraid, I Trust in You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Miktam from Gath: hounded all day, yet the refrain of faith — 'in God I trust… what can man do to me?'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 56 – They Twist My Words
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The conspiracy of foes who lurk for his life, met with the plea to cast down the nations in anger.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 56 – My Tears in Your Bottle
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's tender record of his wanderings (8) and the renewed refrain of trust without fear (9-11).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 56 – Walk Before God in the Light of Life
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Vows of thanksgiving for a soul delivered from death and feet kept from stumbling.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 57 – In the Shadow of Your Wings
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Miktam from the cave: refuge under God's wings until danger passes, the Most High who fulfills His purpose; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 57 – My Soul Among Lions
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Surrounded by men with sword-tongues (4); the refrain 'be exalted, O God' (5); the foes fallen into their own pit (6); Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 57 – Awake, My Glory!
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The steadfast heart roused to song — harp and lyre summoned to 'awaken the dawn.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 57 – I Will Praise You Among the Nations
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Praise widening to the peoples, devotion reaching the heavens, sealed by the repeated 'be exalted, O God.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 58 – Do You Indeed Speak Justly, O Rulers?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Indictment of corrupt judges who devise injustice in their hearts and deal out violence.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 58 – Venom Like a Cobra
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The wicked estranged from the womb, deaf as a snake refusing the charmer's tune.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 58 – Shatter Their Teeth, O God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Imprecation that the lions' fangs be torn out and they melt away like water, a slug, a stillbirth.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 58 – A Reward for the Righteous
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God sweeps them away before the pot feels the thorns (9); the righteous rejoice that 'there is a God who judges the earth' (10-11).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 59 – Deliver Me from My Enemies
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Prayer as Saul watched David's house: fierce men lie in wait for no fault of his own.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 59 – Rouse Yourself to Help Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The cry to the LORD of Hosts to awake and visit the treacherous nations; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 59 – Snarling Like Dogs
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The foes prowling the city with swords in their lips (6-7), met by the God who laughs at the nations (8).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 59 – You Are My Fortress
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The refrain of watching for God his strength, who in devotion comes to meet him.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 59 – That God Rules over Jacob
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Prayer to scatter and consume the proud so the ends of the earth know that God rules; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 59 – They Prowl for Food
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The dog-refrain returns: foes scavenging and growling, unsatisfied.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 59 – I Will Sing of Your Strength in the Morning
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing contrast: morning song to the fortress and refuge in times of trouble.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 60 – You Have Rejected Us, O God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Communal lament after a hard campaign: God has broken and shaken the land — 'restore us!'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 60 – A Banner for Those Who Fear You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The raised standard and the plea to save with God's right hand that His beloved be delivered; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 60 – God Has Spoken from His Sanctuary
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The divine oracle of ownership: Shechem, Gilead, Ephraim, Judah — 'Moab is My washbasin… over Philistia I shout.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 60 – With God We Will Triumph
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Who will lead to Edom? (9-10) The confession that human help is worthless and only with God comes valor (11-12).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 61 – Lead Me to the Rock Higher Than I
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: From the ends of the earth a faint heart calls to its refuge, longing to dwell in God's tent forever; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 61 – Enthroned in God's Presence Forever
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God has heard his vows and given the heritage of those who fear Him; prayer for the king's long, guarded reign.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 62 – In God Alone My Soul Finds Rest
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The opening creed of stillness: He alone is rock, salvation, and fortress — 'I will never be shaken.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 62 – Like a Leaning Wall
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The assault of foes who bless with their mouths but curse within, plotting to topple him; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 62 – Rest in God Alone, O My Soul
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The refrain renewed as self-exhortation: salvation, honor, and refuge all rest on God the strong rock.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 62 – Pour Out Your Hearts Before Him
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Counsel to the people to trust at all times (8), for men are vapor and stolen riches worthless (9-10); Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 62 – Power and Devotion Belong to God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing twofold revelation: strength and steadfast love are His, and He repays each according to his deeds.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 63 – My Soul Thirsts for You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: From the Wilderness of Judah: thirst in a dry land (1), the sanctuary vision (2), and blessing God while life lasts (3-4).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 63 – My Soul Clings to You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Satisfied as with rich food (5), night-watch meditation (6), joy in the shadow of His wings, upheld by His right hand (7-8).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 63 – The King Will Rejoice in God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The fate of those who seek his life — a portion for foxes — against the rejoicing king and the silencing of liars.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 64 – Hide Me from the Secret Plots
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Lament against a mob who sharpen tongues like swords and ambush the innocent without fear.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 64 – Who Will See Them?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The conspirators emboldened in their hidden scheme, certain the depths of the heart cannot be searched.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 64 – But God Will Shoot Them
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The sudden reversal: God's arrow strikes, their own tongues turn on them (7-8), and all mankind fears while the righteous rejoice (9-10).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 65 – Praise Awaits You in Zion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Thanksgiving hymn: the God who hears prayer and atones for transgressions; blessed are those brought to dwell in His courts.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 65 – The Hope of All the Ends of the Earth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Awesome deeds of salvation (5); the God who formed the mountains and stilled the roaring seas and nations (6-7), feared to earth's ends (8).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 65 – You Crown the Year with Bounty
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Providence over the land: watered furrows, the streams of God, the year crowned with overflowing paths of plenty.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 65 – The Hills Are Robed with Joy
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The harvest doxology: pastures and valleys decked with flocks and grain — 'they shout in triumph; indeed, they sing.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 66 – Make a Joyful Noise, All the Earth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Call to universal praise of God's awesome deeds before which His enemies cower; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 66 – He Turned the Sea into Dry Land
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: 'Come and see the works of God' — the Exodus crossing remembered, the eternal Ruler watching the nations; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 66 – You Brought Us into Abundance
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The communal testimony of testing — refined like silver, led through fire and water — yet brought to a place of plenty.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 66 – I Will Fulfill My Vows to You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The turn to personal worship: burnt offerings and vows spoken in distress now paid; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 66 – Come and Listen, I Will Declare
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The witness to all who fear God (16-17): unconfessed sin would have blocked the prayer, but God has surely heard (18-20).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 67 – May God Be Gracious to Us
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Aaronic-blessing echo (1, Selah) so that His salvation is known among all nations, who are called to be glad (2-4); Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 67 – Let All the Peoples Praise You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The refrain renewed (5) and the harvest blessing that the ends of the earth may fear Him (6-7).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 68 – God Arises, His Enemies Scattered
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The processional war-hymn opens with the ark-formula: as smoke and wax vanish, so the wicked perish, but the righteous rejoice.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 68 – A Father of the Fatherless
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Praise to the cloud-Rider whose name is the LORD, defender of widows, who settles the lonely in families.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 68 – When You Marched Through the Wasteland
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Sinai theophany remembered (7-8, Selah) and the abundant rain refreshing His weary inheritance (9-10).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 68 – Kings of Armies Flee
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The women proclaim the victory and divide plunder (11-12); the dove with silver wings; kings scattered like snow on Zalmon (13-14).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 68 – The Mountain God Chose
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Why does mighty Bashan gaze in envy at Zion, the modest peak where the LORD will dwell forever?

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 68 – You Ascended on High
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's myriad chariots (17) and the ascent leading captives and receiving gifts (18), cited of Christ's ascension in Eph 4.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 68 – He Daily Bears Our Burden
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The doxological pause: blessed be the Lord, the God of deliverance and rescue from death; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 68 – God Will Crush the Heads of His Foes
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The renewed war-oracle bringing enemies up from Bashan and the depths of the sea to judgment.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 68 – Your Procession into the Sanctuary
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The festival march seen: singers and musicians among tambourine-maidens, with Benjamin, Judah, Zebulun, and Naphtali.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 68 – Kings Will Bring You Gifts
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Prayer to summon God's strength (28-29) and rebuke the warlike nations until envoys come from Egypt and Cush (30-31).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 68 – Ascribe Power to God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing summons to the kingdoms to sing (32-33, Selah) and ascribe strength to the One awesome in His sanctuary (34-35).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 69 – The Waters Are Up to My Neck
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The great lament opens: sunk in miry depths, weary with crying, eyes failing while looking for God.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 69 – Hated Without Cause
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Foes outnumber the hairs of his head (4); confessed folly (5); the plea that none who hope in God be shamed through him (6).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 69 – Zeal for Your House Has Consumed Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Scorn endured for God's sake, a stranger to his brothers, the verse John applies to Christ cleansing the temple (9).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 69 – The Song of Drunkards
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Mourning and sackcloth turned to mockery; the gossip of those at the gate and the songs of drunkards.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 69 – Rescue Me from the Mire
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The turn to petition for a time of favor: deliver from the deep waters, let not the Pit close its mouth.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 69 – Hide Not Your Face from Your Servant
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Urgent appeal to the God of good devotion to draw near and redeem in the face of his foes.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 69 – Gall for Food, Vinegar for Thirst
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The reproach that broke his heart, with the line fulfilled at the cross — 'they gave me vinegar to quench my thirst.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 69 – May Their Table Become a Snare
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The imprecation begins: darkened eyes and bent backs, God's burning wrath poured out on the persecutors.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 69 – Blotted Out of the Book of Life
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Their tents deserted (25, cited of Judas in Acts 1) and their names erased from the register of the righteous.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 69 – I Will Praise God's Name in Song
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The vow of thanksgiving that pleases the LORD more than any sacrificial bull.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 69 – Let Heaven and Earth Praise Him
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The humble revived because the LORD listens to the needy; all creation summoned to praise.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 69 – God Will Save Zion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing hope of restored cities of Judah inherited by the servants who love His name.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 70 – Make Haste to Deliver Me
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Urgent appeal (mirroring 40:13-17): shame for those who seek his life, joy for those who seek God, 'O LORD, do not delay.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 71 – In You I Take Refuge
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The aged saint's prayer opens: 'be my rock of refuge, where I can always go,' never to be put to shame.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 71 – My Confidence from My Youth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Deliverance sought from the unjust, leaning on God since birth — 'My praise is always for You.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 71 – Do Not Cast Me Off in Old Age
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A portent to many yet sheltered in God (7-8), with the plea not to be forsaken when strength fails (9).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 71 – My Enemies Say God Has Forsaken Him
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The foes who plot, certain there is none to rescue, answered by 'be not far from me, O God.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 71 – But I Will Always Hope
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Prayer that accusers be shamed (13) set against the resolve to hope and 'praise You more and more' (14).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 71 – Your Righteousness All Day Long
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: A mouth declaring God's measureless righteousness and salvation, coming in the strength of the Lord GOD.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 71 – Until I Proclaim to the Next Generation
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Taught from youth, the gray-headed saint asks to live to declare God's power to those yet to come.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 71 – Who, O God, Is Like You?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's righteousness reaching the heavens (19); the confidence that He who showed many troubles will revive and restore (20-21).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 71 – I Will Sing with the Harp
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing vow of joyful praise from redeemed lips and tongue, his accusers disgraced.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 72 – Endow the King with Your Justice
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Solomon's royal psalm: prayer that the king judge the afflicted with righteousness and crush the oppressor.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 72 – Like Rain on the Mown Grass
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: His reign feared as long as sun and moon endure, refreshing as showers, the righteous flourishing in his days.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 72 – From Sea to Sea
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The universal dominion: nomads bowing, kings of Tarshish and Sheba bringing tribute, all nations serving him.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 72 – He Delivers the Needy
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The heart of the king's justice: pity for the poor, redemption from oppression, for their blood is precious in his sight.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 72 – May His Name Endure Forever
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Blessing of long life and abundant grain, his everlasting name in which all nations are blessed.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 72 – Blessed Be His Glorious Name
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The doxology closing Book II — 'may all the earth be filled with His glory. Amen and amen' — with the colophon ending the prayers of David (20).

stories.story_title: Book III – The Crisis of Faith
stories.why_start_end_and_literary_glue: Psalms 73–89 constitute the darkest section—Asaphite laments (73–83) and national crises (74, 79, 89) wrestling with covenant and theodicy. Start (73:1): 'Truly God is good...' End (89:52): doxology 'Amen and Amen.' Literary Glue: national lament and questioning within curated collections.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 73 – I Envied the Arrogant
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Asaph's theodicy opens: God is good to the pure in heart, yet his feet nearly slipped from envy of the prosperous wicked.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 73 – Pride Their Necklace
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The ease of the wicked — no struggle in death, well-fed bodies, clothed in violence.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 73 – Mouths Against the Heavens
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Their iniquity overflowing, arrogant threats, tongues that strut across the earth.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 73 – How Can God Know?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The wicked drinking abundance and scoffing that the Most High has no knowledge — 'always carefree as they increase their wealth.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 73 – Have I Kept My Heart Pure in Vain?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The crisis of faith: afflicted every morning, tempted to speak the doubt that would betray God's children.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 73 – Until I Entered God's Sanctuary
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The turning point of the whole psalm: in the sanctuary he finally discerns the end of the wicked.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 73 – Set on Slick Ground
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The revelation of their ruin — swept away in a moment of terror, despised like a dream on waking.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 73 – Yet I Am Always with You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Confession of his beastly bitterness (21-22) answered by the held hand and the guidance that ends in glory (23-24).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 73 – My Portion Forever
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The summit: 'Whom have I in heaven but You?' — though flesh and heart fail, God is the strength of his heart.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 73 – It Is Good to Draw Near to God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The resolution: the faithless perish, but his refuge is nearness to the Lord GOD, to proclaim His works.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 74 – Why Have You Rejected Us Forever?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Communal lament over a ruined sanctuary: 'remember Your congregation… Mount Zion, where You dwell.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 74 – They Burned Your Sanctuary
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The desecration: foes roaring in the meeting place, smashing carvings, burning every place where God met them.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 74 – No Prophet, No One Knows How Long
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The desolation of silence, the taunting enemy, and the cry, 'why do You withdraw Your right hand?'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 74 – You Crushed the Heads of Leviathan
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The turn to creation-faith: God my King of old who split the sea and broke the dragons' heads.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 74 – Yours Is the Day and the Night
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Creator who set fountain and river, moon and sun, the boundaries of earth, summer and winter.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 74 – Remember How the Enemy Mocked
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Petition that God remember the scoffing foe and the covenant, not give His dove to the beasts.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 74 – Rise Up, O God, Defend Your Cause
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing appeal that the oppressed not retreat in shame, against the ever-rising uproar of His enemies.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 75 – It Is I Who Bear Up Its Pillars
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Thanksgiving for God's nearness (1) and His own voice: He sets the time for judgment and upholds the quaking earth; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 75 – Do Not Lift Up Your Horn
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The warning to the proud, for exaltation comes from no point of the compass.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 75 – The Cup in the Hand of the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God the Judge who brings down and exalts, pouring the foaming wine of wrath for the wicked to drain to the dregs.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 75 – The Horns of the Righteous Exalted
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The closing vow of praise and the divine word cutting off the horns of the wicked.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 76 – God Is Known in Judah
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Zion-hymn: His dwelling in Salem, where He shattered the flashing arrows and weapons of war; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 76 – Horse and Rider Lie Stunned
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: More majestic than the mountains of prey; at the rebuke of the God of Jacob the valiant sleep their last sleep.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 76 – Who Can Stand Before You?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The fear of God who from heaven pronounced judgment to save the lowly, and the earth was still; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 76 – Even the Wrath of Man Shall Praise You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The God who is to be feared, to whom vows are paid and tribute brought, who breaks the spirits of princes.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 77 – My Soul Refused to Be Comforted
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Lament: crying aloud in the day of trouble, the soul unconsoled, the spirit faint at remembering God; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 77 – Too Troubled to Speak
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Sleepless eyes; the turn to consider the days of old and to muse with his heart in the night.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 77 – Has God Forgotten to Be Gracious?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The sharpest questions of faith — 'Is His loving devotion gone forever?' — the crisis at the psalm's center; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 77 – I Will Remember the Works of the LORD
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The deliberate pivot: appealing to memory of the LORD's wonders and mighty deeds of old.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 77 – What God Is So Great as Our God?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: His holy way; the God who works wonders and redeemed the sons of Jacob with power; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 77 – The Waters Saw You and Swirled
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The storm-theophany of the Exodus: thunder, lightning arrows, the trembling earth.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 77 – Your Path Through the Sea
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The unseen footprints through the mighty waters as He led His flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – Tell the Next Generation
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The historical Maskil opens: parables of old not hidden from the children but declared to the coming generation.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – That They Set Their Hope in God
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The purpose of the testimony — that children not be like their stubborn, rebellious fathers.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – The Archers of Ephraim Turned Back
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The indictment: they broke God's covenant and forgot the wonders He had shown them.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – He Split the Sea and the Rock
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The Exodus wonders before their fathers: the divided sea like a wall, water gushing from the stone.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – Can God Prepare a Table?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Yet they sinned, testing God by craving food — 'can He also give bread… meat?'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – The Bread of Angels
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Wrath kindled at their unbelief (21-22), yet He opened heaven's doors and rained down manna (23-25).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – Meat Like Dust
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The east wind driving quail like sand of the sea, so they ate and were well filled.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – With the Food Still in Their Mouths
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Judgment in the midst of craving: the strongest struck down, their days ended in futility.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – They Flattered Him with Their Mouths
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Shallow repentance: they sought their Rock yet lied with their tongues, hearts disloyal to His covenant.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – Yet He Was Compassionate
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The mercy that restrained full wrath, remembering they were but flesh, a passing breeze.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – How Often They Grieved Him
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The wilderness pattern of testing the Holy One, forgetting the day of redemption from the adversary.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – His Signs in the Fields of Zoan
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The plagues recalled: rivers to blood, devouring swarms of flies, devastating frogs.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – Crops to the Locust
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The locust, the killing hail on vines and sycamores, lightning on the livestock.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – A Band of Destroying Angels
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The unleashed fury and the climactic plague — all the firstborn struck in the tents of Ham.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – Led Like a Flock to the Holy Land
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Shepherded safely through the sea that engulfed their foes, settled in the inheritance He apportioned.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – Twisted Like a Faulty Bow
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Yet they tested Him in the land, provoking jealousy with high places and idols.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – He Abandoned Shiloh
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's fury rejecting Israel, forsaking the tabernacle, delivering His strength to captivity.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – Priests Fell by the Sword
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: His people surrendered to the sword; young men, maidens, and priests consumed, with no songs to mourn.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – Then the Lord Awoke
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God rousing like a warrior to beat back His foes, rejecting the tent of Joseph and Ephraim.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – He Chose Mount Zion
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The election of Judah and Zion, His sanctuary built like the heights, established forever.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 78 – He Chose David His Servant
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The climactic choice: David taken from the sheepfolds to shepherd Israel with integrity of heart.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 79 – They Have Reduced Jerusalem to Rubble
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: National lament: the temple defiled, corpses unburied, Israel a reproach to its neighbors.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 79 – How Long, O LORD?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The cry against God's burning jealousy and the plea to pour wrath on the nations that devoured Jacob.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 79 – Atone for Our Sins, for Your Name's Sake
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Appeal to compassion and the glory of His name — 'why should the nations ask, Where is their God?'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 79 – The Sheep of Your Pasture Will Thank You
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Plea for the captives and sevenfold requital, closing in a vow of generations-long praise.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 80 – Hear Us, O Shepherd of Israel
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The opening cry to the cherubim-enthroned Shepherd and the first sounding of the refrain: 'Restore us… that we may be saved.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 80 – The Bread of Tears
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: How long the smoldering anger (4); fed with tears and mocked by neighbors (5-6); the refrain repeated (7).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 80 – You Brought a Vine Out of Egypt
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The allegory of the vine: transplanted, taking root, filling the land to the Sea and the River.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 80 – Why Have You Broken Down Its Walls?
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The vine now ravaged by the boar; the plea, 'Return, O God of Hosts… attend to this vine.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 80 – Revive Us, and We Will Call on Your Name
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The vine cut and burned (16); the hand upon the man at God's right hand (17-18); the final refrain (19).

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 81 – Sound the Ram's Horn at the Feast
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: Festival summons to sing and play, for it is a statute and ordinance of the God of Jacob.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 81 – I Relieved His Shoulder of the Burden
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's voice recalling the Exodus deliverance and the testing at the waters of Meribah; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 81 – Open Wide Your Mouth
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The covenant plea: no strange god among them — 'I am the LORD your God… I will fill it.'

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 81 – But My People Would Not Listen
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The tragedy of refusal: given up to their stubborn hearts, with the LORD's grieving wish that they would listen.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 81 – Honey from the Rock
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: The promise spurned: how soon He would subdue their foes and satisfy them with the finest wheat.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 82 – God Presides in the Divine Assembly
scenes.why_start_end_and_devices: God's indictment of the unjust 'gods': 'how long will you judge unjustly?' — defend the weak and fatherless; Selah.

scenes.scene_name: Psalm 82 – Like Mortals You Will Die
